Subject: MAP kickoff: need to lock tokens/$ + caching & batching assumptions

Hey Kimberly & Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and our ML team asked for a concise section in the MAP that spells out the unit economics assumptions we used to size the pilot and the quoted pricing. Specifically:

- tokens per user/session assumptions (avg and 95th)
- any prefix / KV caching expected and hit-rate assumptions
- batching/throughput assumptions + latency SLO tradeoffs

Can you send the version of the MAP that includes those figures and the evaluation plan timeline? Our finance lead wants this for the internal sign-off (they'll sign off on the pilot if the unit economics check out).

Also, procurement will need a short doc that maps these assumptions to the expected monthly cost at 10k DAU and a procurement-friendly file for the SOW.

Thanks — can we get a draft by EOD Tuesday (7/15)?

—Michael

Head of Data & ML, PulseCare

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Michael Lee <michael.lee@pulsecare.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: need to lock tokens/$ + caching & batching assumptions

Michael —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attaching a first-pass XLSX (pulsecare_map_cost_assumptions_v1.xlsx) and a short note on prefetch/padding vs. batch sizing (redwood-prefetch-batching-note.pdf). Quick summary below so procurement has something to circulate immediately:

- Tokens/session (baseline): 750 tokens avg / 2,400 tokens p95. We modeled both a conservative and an optimistic path in the sheet (tabs: baseline / optimistic).
- Caching: We recommend prefix KV caching for prompt templates & static user context. We used a 38% hit rate for conservative model and 62% for optimistic; details in sheet (cache_hit_assumptions tab).
- Batching: We modeled 3 strategies — small-batch (4 reqs, target p99 latency 220ms), medium-batch (8 reqs, p99 ~320ms), and throughput mode (16+ reqs, p99 degrades but cost/token improves). Our MAP baseline assumes medium-batch for user-facing flows and throughput mode for background jobs.

Evaluation plan (high-level):
- Week 0–2: baseline telemetry capture & synthetic replay (validate tokens/session)
- Week 3–4: Canary with 5% traffic (measure real cache hit rates and latency)
- Week 5: Evaluate cost vs. latency and finalize pilot SLOs

Timeline note: We can deliver the updated MAP and the procurement-friendly SOW file by EOD 2025-07-15 as requested.

Open questions for you:
1) For the 10k DAU projection — is the user distribution skewed (heavy power users) or roughly uniform? That changes p95 substantially.
2) Any hard p99 latency requirement? We used 350ms as an internal cutoff for interactive flows.

I'll loop Neha on the billing cadence / credits for the pilot. Ben will validate the batching numbers once he confirms the target instance sizing.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: need to lock tokens/$ + caching & batching assumptions

Quick follow-up — a few operational clarifications that affect unit economics:

- Prefetch vs. cache: if PulseCare prefers deterministic low-latency for first-token responses we should budget for a higher reserved capacity and assume lower effective cache hit rates (we modeled that in the conservative tab).
- Batching sensitivity: the sheet includes a sensitivity table showing cost/token improvements at 8x and 16x batching. Important to note: medium-batch (8 reqs) gives ~22% cost improvement vs small-batch with only ~100ms median latency increase in our testbed.
- KV eviction policy: we assumed LRU with 48h TTL for session artifacts; if you need longer retention the memory pressure will increase instance footprint.

Action items I'm taking:
- Validate the medium-batch p99 numbers on the infra cluster (will update the sheet with observed p99 across two instance classes).
- Add a small appendix that maps each assumption to procurement language (e.g., "tokens per call" -> line item in cost schedule).

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Lee <michael.lee@pulsecare.com>

Thanks Kimberly & Ben — this is exactly what we needed. Procurement reviewed the XLSX and the summary appendix (procurement attached). A couple quick confirmations before we finalize the MAP:

- We will assume the conservative cache hit rates (38%) for the SOW pricing; if live canary shows >50% we'll renegotiate the post-pilot unit price per the MAP clause.
- PulseCare requires p99 <= 400ms for core patient-facing flows — based on your notes medium-batch looks acceptable.
- Procurement asked that the SOW include an explicit note about prefetched tokens (you have a line in the appendix) so legal can sign off on how we count prefetched vs generated tokens.

Please bundle the final MAP + SOW-ready file and send to procurement@pulsecare.com; procurement will share DocuSign next week.

Agreement to timeline: final MAP + SOW sent by close of business today will allow procurement to start signatures Monday.

—Michael
